_comment: Issue #85 increment 1: seek previews. Subject is the header-only src/core/Trickplay.h -- the tile lookup (which grid, row and column a second of film is in, including the SHORT last grid and a time past the end), the path+mtime+size cache key that makes a replaced file lose its old strip, the resume point of an interrupted walk, the LRU eviction order, the sidecar's strictness, and the guard that keeps generation off anything that is not a file on this machine. probe_trickplay asserts them.

mutants.name: a-stream-is-previewed
mutants._why: THE decision of this increment, restated as a mutation: a url stops being refused. Generating previews means seeking a file three hundred times, so on a debrid link that is three hundred range requests against the user's quota -- for a courtesy nobody asked for. The issue names this as the scope guard and the brief calls for a predicate rather than an if somebody can move.

mutants.name: a-network-share-is-previewed
mutants._why: A UNC path is a file we CAN read and must not: pulling a whole film across SMB to make thumbnails is the same bargain the http refusal declines, paid in someone else's bandwidth. It is the refusal most easily argued away, so it is the one worth a mutant.

mutants.name: a-drive-letter-is-read-as-a-scheme
mutants._why: The one-letter rule gone. 'C:' becomes a protocol, so every file on Windows is classified as a stream and the feature silently never generates anything -- a total, invisible failure that a Linux-only test would never see.

mutants.name: the-key-ignores-mtime
mutants._why: Jellyfin 10.11's own lesson deleted. A replaced file keeps the previous film's thumbnails, so the strip shows one movie while the player shows another, with the timestamps still looking authoritative. The issue names this as the thing to bake in from day one.

mutants.name: the-key-ignores-size
mutants._why: mtime alone misses the replacement that PRESERVED the timestamp -- rsync -t, a restore from backup, an archiver -- which is exactly the tool most likely to have changed the bytes underneath us. Size is the second half of the same guarantee.

mutants.name: path-separators-are-identity
mutants._why: Without normalisation the same file opened as 'D:\Films\x.mkv' and as 'D:/Films/x.mkv' is two cache items: the strip is generated twice, stored twice, and counted twice against the size bound.

mutants.name: the-last-grid-is-treated-as-full
mutants._why: A film is never a whole number of grids. Assuming the final sheet is full makes the tail of every single file wrong -- and only the tail, which is where nobody looks.

mutants.name: a-short-grid-is-written-full-height
mutants._why: A 3-frame tail of a 5x5 sheet stored as five rows is 25x the bytes for nothing, and the blit reads rows of black past the last real frame.

mutants.name: a-time-past-the-end-is-not-clamped
mutants._why: A drag lands a hair past the reported duration routinely (a VBR file over-reports by a frame or two). Unclamped, the lookup falls off the end of the sheet and the scrub shows a BLANK at exactly the moment the user is aiming at the end of the film.

mutants.name: row-and-column-are-swapped
mutants._why: The failure this feature cannot survive: the thumbnail is of a DIFFERENT second of the film, under a confident timestamp. Nothing on screen says so -- it is a plausible frame from the same movie -- and the seek it invites lands somewhere else.
mutants.find:
t.row = within / l.cols;
    t.col = within % l.cols;
mutants.replace:
t.row = within % l.cols;
    t.col = within / l.cols;

mutants.name: the-tail-of-a-file-gets-no-frame
mutants._why: Floor instead of ceil: a 25 s file at 10 s intervals earns two frames instead of three, so the last stretch of EVERY file has no preview at all -- the strip just stops before the end.

mutants.name: resume-counts-instead-of-finding-the-hole
mutants._why: A directory holding grids 0, 1 and 3 (grid 2 lost to a failed rename) must resume at 2. Counting what is present instead answers 4, so the gap is never filled and that film has a hole in its strip forever.

mutants.name: a-broken-sidecar-is-accepted
mutants._why: A truncated or hand-edited sidecar describing a zero interval must read as 'no previews'. Accepted instead, the very next tile lookup divides by zero on a user's machine -- and the sidecar is read on every open.

mutants.name: a-future-sidecar-version-is-read-as-v1
mutants._why: The version field is the only way a later layout change can invalidate today's caches. Ignored, a v2 sidecar is read with v1's field meanings and every frame is looked up in the wrong place.

mutants.name: a-sidecar-may-claim-grids-that-do-not-exist
mutants._why: completeGrids is the resume point and the player's 'how much of this strip exists'. Unchecked, a corrupt count sends the reader after grid files that were never written, once per scrub.

mutants.name: eviction-does-not-stop-at-the-bound
mutants._why: The sweep empties the cache instead of trimming it to fit, so every item is regenerated on the next open -- a background job that keeps the disk busy forever, which is precisely the manner the issue asks for.

mutants.name: eviction-takes-the-item-in-hand
mutants._why: Deleting the strip of the file being watched -- or the half-finished grids of the file the job is walking -- turns a size bound into a loop that generates and destroys the same work forever.

mutants.name: eviction-takes-the-newest-first
mutants._why: MRU instead of LRU: the cache keeps what you will never open again and throws away what you were watching last night. The bound is respected and the cache is worthless.

mutants.name: a-tie-is-broken-the-other-way
mutants._why: Two items last used in the same second have to evict in a fixed order or the same cache state gives different answers on two runs -- and then nothing about eviction is testable, which is how an eviction bug survives a green suite.
